text:
Priya: Quick q — trying to add my domestic partner to medical + dental after we moved in together. Is there a deadline for submitting docs for a 2026-04-01 effective date? What paperwork do you need? thanks! :pray:

Sam (People Ops): Congrats, @Priya! You have 30 days from the qualifying life event (move-in) to submit for a mid-cycle enrollment. Effective date is usually the date of the move-in if docs are dated within those 30 days, otherwise the first of the next month. If you want 4/1, submit by 3/31 and include dated proof.

Priya: Thanks — what counts as "proof" exactly? Lease shows move-in on 2/14 but joint bank acct just opened. Do we need both?

Ben (Benefits): Hi all — acceptable docs: one of the following: signed domestic partnership affidavit (preferred), joint lease/mortgage with both names + move-in date, joint bank/utility statement dated within the 30-day window, or a locally-registered partnership certificate where applicable. If you have the DP affidavit + one supporting doc that's usually enough. Notarization helps but not mandatory.

Priya: Got it. Is there a form somewhere? How do I actually submit?

Sam (People Ops): Submit through Workday: Benefits > Change Life Event > Add Dependent. Attach PDFs of the docs. If you prefer, DM me the filenames and I can check the upload. Also set the coverage selections before you submit so payroll updates immediately if premiums change.

Jamal: Quick tax/legal note — domestic partner premiums may be imputed income on your W-2 if partner isn't a tax dependent. Ben, can you confirm?

Ben (Benefits): Correct — if partner doesn't qualify as a tax dependent, the value of employer-paid premiums for partner coverage is considered imputed income. We send a benefits tax notice. If that's a concern DM me and we can run a quick estimate.

Priya: How long until ID cards are issued? We have an appointment next week.

Ben (Benefits): Once enrollment is processed, the carrier typically issues ID cards in 7–10 business days. If you need proof immediately, we can generate a benefits verification letter from the portal (PDF) that shows effective date and coverage — that's accepted at most clinics.

Priya: Perfect. One more — can coverage be backdated to the move-in date if I miss the 30-day window but can show other docs earlier?

Sam (People Ops): Retro coverage exceptions are rare and need case review. If you missed the 30-day window, submit anyway and choose "retro effective date" in Workday and add a note. We'll escalate to the carrier for review but no guarantees.

Priya: Thanks everyone — submitting now. @Sam I'll DM the files in a sec.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: Benefits change request received. Ticket #B-2026-312 created. Expect processing within 3 business days. Link: https://benefits.example.com/portal/tickets/B-2026-312

Sam (People Ops): Got the DM, @Priya. I'll flag it for expedited review given your appointment. :thumbsup:

Priya: You're the best, thanks :heart:
